title: Book your pre-review 1:1
why_matters: The pre-review 1:1 is what makes the review itself boring — which is the outcome you want. Five to seven days before the formal review, you share the self-assessment with your manager and ask whether there's anything they'd flag now that they'd rather not surface in the room. Surprises in the review are a failure of preparation.
steps: Book a fifteen-minute 1:1 with your manager, between five and seven days before your formal review.
Send the self-assessment 24 hours before the meeting. Ask one specific question in the calendar invite: "is there anything you'd want to flag that you'd rather not surface in the review itself?".
In the meeting, listen. Take notes. Resist the urge to defend.
Within four hours of the meeting, update your self-assessment based on what you heard. Note in your evidence file what was raised + what you'll do about it.
success_criteria: Pre-review meeting is booked and the self-assessment has been shared 24 hours ahead. After the meeting, the assessment has been updated and the discussion is summarised in your evidence file.
reflection_prompt: What did your manager say that you didn't anticipate, and what does it change about how you'll go into the formal review?
